question: Using the inverse-matrix method, solve $4x+y=9$ and $3x+y=7$. Hence, calculate $2x-y$.
explanation:
Matrix equation
$$\begin{bmatrix}4&1\\3&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}9\\7\end{bmatrix}$$
Inverse of the coefficient matrix
The determinant is $1$, so $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-3&4\end{bmatrix}$$
Solution matrix
$$X=A^{-1}B=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-3&4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}9\\7\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
Required expression
Therefore, $$2x-y=2(2)-1=3$$
